solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Braves declare it avoids humiliation

parts.note: to brave danger is to face it, so braves means faces
to aver is to declare or state firmly

explanation.surface: A sports team called the Braves announces it has dodged an embarrassing defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braves' looks like a team name but is a verb: faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that saves face spares a person embarrassment or loss of dignity.

clue.text: Beat sailor getting the biscuit

parts.note: to flap wings is to beat them
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor beats others to get the last biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a chewy oat bar, sold alongside biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: The British oat-and-syrup bar is a sweet baked snack treated as a biscuit.

clue.text: Settler Mark is going to Thailand

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
taken as written
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A settler called Mark is moving to Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name but is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who settles in a new territory.

clue.text: Net South American part of 19

parts.note: a gene is one unit of the hereditary information at 19-down

explanation.surface: A net from South America, forming part of another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagene is a type of fishing net, a dictionary-only word.

clue.text: Nameless furious lady

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: furious means violent

explanation.surface: An anonymous woman flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a woman's first name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Philosopher found in women's clothing, topless

indicators.note: topless means losing its first letter, here the top of the clothing word in a down clue

parts.note: a trousseau is a bride's collection of clothes

explanation.surface: A thinker is discovered dressed in women's clothes with no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of TROUSSEAU, a bride's outfit and linens.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century Genevan thinker behind The Social Contract.

clue.text: Go round double speed

indicators.note: double says the letter for round appears twice in a row

parts.note: a round shape is O
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: An instruction to go round a track at twice the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means energy or drive, the same as vigour or zest.

clue.text: Performing definite duty at work

parts.note: an actor who is performing is on stage, on
the is the definite article
a job is a duty or task

explanation.surface: Someone carrying out a set task while at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged in their occupation is working, at their post.

clue.text: Unwholesome condition of youngster during month

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the youngster goes inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young person falls ill in a particular month.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or disorder, an unhealthy state.

clue.text: The man would take food in warmed

indicators.note: in tells us the eating word goes inside the contraction

parts.note: the man would contracts to he'd
to take food is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A man would take food in once it had been warmed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'take food in' but is the container signal; the contraction of 'the man would' does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated means warmed up, raised in temperature.

clue.text: Cheerful, notedly so

definitions.meaning: the Italian word means merry or cheerful
in musical notation it directs a brisk, lively tempo

explanation.surface: Someone who is cheerful in a remarkable way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notedly' hides 'in musical notes': the same word as a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word literally means merry, and as a tempo marking asks for lively, bright playing.

clue.text: Become despondent having three also involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of three also are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone grows gloomy because three other people have got mixed up in the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow despondent is to give up hope, losing courage and spirit.

clue.text: A book about fruit providing nourishment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so A and the book go around the fruit

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A cookery book about fruit that offers nourishing recipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is food, so it is what provides nourishment; the definition is loose in part of speech but the sense is nutrition.

clue.text: Appreciated lady was in dire need

indicators.note: was in says one piece sits inside the other
dire means dreadful, signalling the letters of need are jumbled into ENED

parts.note: Joy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady who was in desperate want was grateful for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady' is a woman's name here, not the definition; the definition is 'Appreciated'.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something is to take pleasure in it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Chipboard Ken cut round cook's facility

indicators.note: round suggests turning the letters about, so Chipboard Ken cut is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ken cuts chipboard to build a unit for the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like the indicator but is fodder; 'round' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen storage unit is a facility the cook uses for pans and food.

clue.text: Henry's playing around in the country

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the letters from Henry's

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance, plus S from the possessive

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of around are fooling about in a new order

explanation.surface: Henry is fooling about somewhere out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The henry is the unit of electrical inductance, symbol H; with the possessive S it makes the outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a nation of Central America.

clue.text: Observant while practically incognito

indicators.note: while is the loose signal that the shortened word is rearranged meanwhile
practically means almost, so incognito loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone notices things while travelling almost unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' drops the last O of INCOGNITO, leaving INCOGNIT, whose letters rearrange; the anagram signal is weak, and 'while' is the only candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being observant means taking notice of what goes on around you, attentive.

clue.text: Renegade petty officer in Utah, say

indicators.note: in tells us the officer goes inside

parts.note: Utah is an example of a US state, a state

explanation.surface: A naval officer in Utah who has abandoned his post.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, a deserter or turncoat.

clue.text: Stride out grasping half ballet-skirt from remains

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the jumbled word encloses the skirt part
out suggests the letters of stride are put out of order
half means only half of the skirt word is kept

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet dancer's skirt

explanation.surface: Someone strides out holding a piece of ballet dress taken from the rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges STRIDE into DETRIS, which, 'grasping' TU (half of TUTU), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste, the leftovers of something broken up.

clue.text: They were wise taking no time to reach the line

parts.note: the Magi were the Wise Men of the Nativity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wise men hurrying to reach a boundary in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: The French defensive fortifications of the 1930s were known as the Maginot Line.
explanation.definitionFit: The French border defences of the 1930s are often called simply the Line, named after war minister André Maginot.

clue.text: Prominent old boat entering sea

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the boat goes into the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Noah's Ark is an ancient boat

explanation.surface: An ancient ship that stands out as it sails into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked means noticeable or conspicuous, standing out clearly.

clue.text: Ring yours truly following up intelligence hereditary info

indicators.note: in a down clue the ring and yours truly follow below, after the intelligence word

parts.note: gen is slang for information or intelligence
a ring is shaped like O
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A cryptic order to give a ring and myself after collecting intelligence on heredity.
explanation.definitionFit: A genome is the full set of genes in an organism, its inherited information.

clue.text: Bachelor Troy leaving gate to be destroyed by fire

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so the letter for Troy departs from the gate word

parts.note: a gate is the number attending an event, the turnout
t is the abbreviation for troy in weights

explanation.surface: A single man named Troy leaves through a gate as fire consumes everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is attendance at a match, TURNOUT; 'leaving' takes away the T for troy (as in troy weight).
explanation.definitionFit: A building that is gutted completely by flames is said to burn out.

clue.text: Move tons using sum of money allowed

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

explanation.surface: Shifting tonnes of material using an allotted sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is an allowance of money set aside for a purpose.

clue.text: Bundle to turn over out of bed

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
someone up has risen from bed

explanation.surface: An order to wrap up, turn over and get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rolled into a cylinder is a bundle; British slang also uses it for a hand-made cigarette.

clue.text: Tear round animal that had given up

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the tear word encloses the animal

parts.note: to rend is to tear
the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A tear appears round an animal that had surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formally abandoned or relinquished has been given up.

clue.text: Brave man in luxury tourer

indicators.note: in says the man sits inside the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, denotes a luxury touring car
Allan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A courageous man sitting in a fancy grand touring car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes someone courageous and spirited, especially in battle.

clue.text: Grounds, say, debtors included

indicators.note: included means held within, so the debtors word contains the example

parts.note: Dr is the accounting abbreviation for debtor, plural Drs
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Reasons given, for example, with people who owe money included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons but means coffee grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the sediment left at the bottom, the leftover residue.

clue.text: Begin to print new posters with energy first

indicators.note: first says the energy word is placed at the front, before the rearranged posters

parts.note: go means energy or drive

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of posters

explanation.surface: A printer starts running off a new batch of posters with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'first' put the energy word ahead of the jumbled posters, though the clue lists them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper or book that goes to press starts being printed.
